# Follow the Rupee

> Transparency dashboard for Mumbai's monsoon road-repair spending. It traces where each ward's 2025 road-repair budget went, audits work orders for overbilling / failed fixes / rain-day excuses, grades contractors, and recommends where the next rupee should go.

This site is open to search engines and AI agents. Pages are server-rendered HTML; the same underlying data is available as JSON through a public API and as static JSON files. IMPORTANT: this is an audit SIMULATION on 100% synthetic data — contractors, complaints, work orders and notices are fictional; figures exist to demonstrate an audit workflow, not to accuse any real person or company.

## Pages

- [/](/): Overview — city-wide spend, flags, and how to read the site.
- [/map](/map): Ward map — click a ward to open its report (interactive Leaflet map).
- [/audit](/audit): Audit desk — flagged work orders with reasons, evidence and amounts at issue; CSV export at [/audit/flags.csv](/audit/flags.csv).
- [/contractors](/contractors): Contractor report cards — grades A–D based on durability, SLA and cost ratios.
- [/heatmap](/heatmap): Risk heatmap — flood hotspots, accidents during pending works, low-lying and tide-sensitive wards.
- [/plan](/plan): Where the next rupee should go — ward-level repair plan ranked by recoverable money and risk.
- [/track](/track): Track a complaint — status and re-open history by complaint / work-order id.
- [/ward/F-S](/ward/F-S): Ward report — one page per ward (24 wards). Codes contain "/", slugs use "-", e.g. ward F/S → /ward/F-S.

## Public JSON API (GET, no auth)

Base URL: the site root. All endpoints return JSON and are open to agents.

- GET /api/wards: all wards with budget, spend and office details. Query params: `zone` (exact match), `search` (free text over ward name / office / localities).
- GET /api/work-orders: work orders with contractor, cost, method and SLA info. Query params: `ward_code`, `contractor_id`, `repair_method` (exact), `sla_met` (Y/N), `limit` (default 100, max 1000), `offset` (paginated).
- GET /api/complaints: complaints with status, language and linked work order. Query params: `ward_code`, `status`, `language`, `channel`, `limit` (default 100, max 1000), `offset`.
- GET /api/audit-flags: audit flag rows with amounts, confidence and per-flag totals. Query params: `ward_code`, `flag`, `confidence`, `limit` (default 500, max 1000), `offset`.
- GET /api/health: database connectivity and table row counts — useful to probe before bulk queries.

`POST /api/ai` is the site's internal assistant endpoint; it requires sign-in and is NOT available to external agents.

## Static JSON data files

Pre-computed analysis snapshots, regenerated by the pipeline (see `meta.note` in each file for the synthetic-data disclaimer):

- [/data/audit_flags.json](/data/audit_flags.json): every flagged work order, reason codes and amounts.
- [/data/contractor_scores.json](/data/contractor_scores.json): contractor grades, weights and evidence.
- [/data/trail_index.json](/data/trail_index.json): complaint-trail integrity index (duplicates, recategorisations, geocoding).
- [/data/ward_simulator.json](/data/ward_simulator.json): ward risk simulation with the flood/accident risk formula.

## Notes for agents

- Currency is Indian Rupees (INR, formatted with the en-IN locale, e.g. ₹1,60,000).
- Ward codes are single letters or letter/letter pairs (A, B, ... F/S, M/W, R/C); URL slugs replace "/" with "-".
- "next rupee" fields describe the recommended allocation for each ward's remaining budget.
- Sitemap: /sitemap.xml. Admin dashboard (/admin) is not crawlable.
